title: Onyx Stage — All-Hands Proclamation
description: A full-bleed ink-black canvas where a single oversized aspirational phrase in bone-white commands total silence. Distinct from hero templates that lean on imagery or gradient fills — authority here comes from absolute negative space.
philosophy: This template is built for the moment a room goes quiet before a leader speaks. It borrows its grammar directly from the great keynote stage: darkness, one idea, nothing competing. It refuses sub-headlines, decorative motifs, background photography, and supporting copy — because presence requires emptiness. It exists for the speaker who has earned the right to say one thing and let it land.
goodFor: Single-phrase vision or theme reveals at annual kick-offs
Stage-projected keynote openers where the speaker walks out to silence
Internal strategic pivot moments requiring emotional weight before detail
avoidFor: Decks shared as async documents without a live presenter to carry the silence
Investor pitch slides where claims need immediate supporting context
Any slide requiring charts, bullet points, or more than one idea
Brand-constrained environments mandating light backgrounds or busy logo lockups
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a darkened auditorium the instant before a leader steps forward — total stillness, expectation heavy in the air. A single aspirational phrase claims the gravitational center of an ink-black field, its bone-white letterforms carrying full compositional weight with nothing competing for attention. The mood is monumental and spare, drawing all authority from what is deliberately absent; avoid any softening through texture, glow, gradient, or decorative marks — presence lives entirely in the surrounding void.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed edge-to-edge canvas with zero outer margins — the dark field has no boundary and bleeds to every edge. A single text element is anchored at the vertical midpoint, spanning cols 3–10 of a 12-col grid to preserve substantial lateral void on both flanks. No header band, no footer, no page number, no rule lines — the only structural element is the lone phrase itself. Hierarchy is achieved by scale contrast alone: one typographic object at maximum size against unbroken empty field.

examples.promptCore: The slide sustains the same charged silence as the opener — deep darkness absorbs the eye while a single dominant statement or attributed quote floats isolated, demanding the room rather than informing it. Compositional rhythm is controlled and unhurried: the main idea carries mass at the optical center, and a faint subordinate line below a fine rule provides the only counterweight, like a breath held just before release. The mood is proclamation-as-theater — weight without clutter, authority without ornament. Avoid any list structure, visual texture, iconography, or layered hierarchy that would fracture the singular focus.

  <text x="1840" y="1020" font-family="ui-monospace, monospace" font-size="14" fill="#5a4f3a" opacity="0.55" text-anchor="end" letter-spacing="3">02 / 24</text>

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with the primary content element — a single stat callout, short quote, or bold proclamation — spanning cols 2–10, placed slightly above vertical center to echo stage-projection convention. Full-bleed dark background, no header band, no footer chrome except a page number pinned bottom-right at near-invisible contrast. A single hairline rule, no thicker than 1px, may separate the main statement from one subordinate line of attribution or context; nothing else occupies the canvas.
